NKJV.1: And the children of Israel, according to their number, the heads of fathers’ houses, the captains of thousands and hundreds and their officers, served the king in every matter of the military divisions. These divisions came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year, each division having twenty-four thousand.
NKJV.2: Over the first division for the first month was Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel, and in his division were twenty-four thousand;
NKJV.3: he was of the children of Perez, and the chief of all the captains of the army for the first month.
NKJV.4: Over the division of the second month was Dodai an Ahohite, and of his division Mikloth also was the leader; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NKJV.5: The third captain of the army for the third month was Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada the priest, who was chief; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NKJV.6: This was the Benaiah who was mighty among the thirty, and was over the thirty; in his division was Ammizabad his son.
NKJV.7: The fourth captain for the fourth month was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NKJV.8: The fifth captain for the fifth month was Shamhuth the Izrahite; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NKJV.9: The sixth captain for the sixth month was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NKJV.10: The seventh captain for the seventh month was Helez the Pelonite, of the children of Ephraim; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NKJV.11: The eighth captain for the eighth month was Sibbechai the Hushathite, of the Zarhites; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NKJV.12: The ninth captain for the ninth month was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjamites; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NKJV.13: The tenth captain for the tenth month was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zarhites; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NKJV.14: The eleventh captain for the eleventh month was Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the children of Ephraim; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NKJV.15: The twelfth captain for the twelfth month was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NKJV.16: Furthermore, over the tribes of Israel: the officer over the Reubenites was Eliezer the son of Zichri; over the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maachah;
NKJV.17: over the Levites, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel; over the Aaronites, Zadok;
NKJV.18: over Judah, Elihu, one of David’s brothers; over Issachar, Omri the son of Michael;
NKJV.19: over Zebulun, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah; over Naphtali, Jerimoth the son of Azriel;
NKJV.20: over the children of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah; over the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah;
NKJV.21: over the half–tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo the son of Zechariah; over Benjamin, Jaasiel the son of Abner;
NKJV.22: over Dan, Azarel the son of Jeroham. These were the leaders of the tribes of Israel.
NKJV.23: But David did not take the number of those twenty years old and under, because the LORD had said He would multiply Israel like the stars of the heavens.
NKJV.24: Joab the son of Zeruiah began a census, but he did not finish, for wrath came upon Israel because of this census; nor was the number recorded in the account of the chronicles of King David.
NKJV.25: And Azmaveth the son of Adiel was over the king’s treasuries; and Jehonathan the son of Uzziah was over the storehouses in the field, in the cities, in the villages, and in the fortresses.
NKJV.26: Ezri the son of Chelub was over those who did the work of the field for tilling the ground.
NKJV.27: And Shimei the Ramathite was over the vineyards, and Zabdi the Shiphmite was over the produce of the vineyards for the supply of wine.
NKJV.28: Baal-Hanan the Gederite was over the olive trees and the sycamore trees that were in the lowlands, and Joash was over the store of oil.
NKJV.29: And Shitrai the Sharonite was over the herds that fed in Sharon, and Shaphat the son of Adlai was over the herds that were in the valleys.
NKJV.30: Obil the Ishmaelite was over the camels, Jehdeiah the Meronothite was over the donkeys,
NKJV.31: and Jaziz the Hagrite was over the flocks. All these were the officials over King David’s property.
NKJV.32: Also Jehonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, a wise man, and a scribe; and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons.
NKJV.33: Ahithophel was the king’s counselor, and Hushai the Archite was the king’s companion.
NKJV.34: After Ahithophel was Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, then Abiathar. And the general of the king’s army was Joab.

NASB.1: Now [this is] the enumeration of the sons of Israel, the heads of fathers' [households], the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in all the affairs of the divisions which came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year, each division [numbering] 24,000:
NASB.2: Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel had charge of the first division for the first month; and in his division [were] 24,000.
NASB.3: [He was] from the sons of Perez, [and was] chief of all the commanders of the army for the first month.
NASB.4: Dodai the Ahohite and his division had charge of the division for the second month, Mikloth [being] the chief officer; and in his division [were] 24,000.
NASB.5: The third commander of the army for the third month [was] Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada the priest, [as] chief; and in his division [were] 24,000.
NASB.6: This Benaiah [was] the mighty man of the thirty, and had charge of thirty; and over his division was Ammizabad his son.
NASB.7: The fourth for the fourth month [was] Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him; and in his division [were] 24,000.
NASB.8: The fifth for the fifth month [was] the commander Shamhuth the Izrahite; and in his division [were] 24,000.
NASB.9: The sixth for the sixth month [was] Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; and in his division [were] 24,000.
NASB.10: The seventh for the seventh month [was] Helez the Pelonite of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division [were] 24,000.
NASB.11: The eighth for the eighth month [was] Sibbecai the Hushathite of the Zerahites; and in his division [were] 24,000.
NASB.12: The ninth for the ninth month [was] Abiezer the Anathothite of the Benjamites; and in his division [were] 24,000.
NASB.13: The tenth for the tenth month [was] Maharai the Netophathite of the Zerahites; and in his division [were] 24,000.
NASB.14: The eleventh for the eleventh month [was] Benaiah the Pirathonite of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division [were] 24,000.
NASB.15: The twelfth for the twelfth month [was] Heldai the Netophathite of Othniel; and in his division [were] 24,000.
NASB.16: Now in charge of the tribes of Israel: chief officer for the Reubenites was Eliezer the son of Zichri; for the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maacah;
NASB.17: for Levi, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;
NASB.18: for Judah, Elihu, [one] of David's brothers; for Issachar, Omri the son of Michael;
NASB.19: for Zebulun, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jeremoth the son of Azriel;
NASB.20: for the sons of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah; for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah;
NASB.21: for the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo the son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel the son of Abner;
NASB.22: for Dan, Azarel the son of Jeroham. These [were] the princes of the tribes of Israel.
NASB.23: But David did not count those twenty years of age and under, because the LORD had said He would multiply Israel as the stars of heaven.
NASB.24: Joab the son of Zeruiah had begun to count [them], but did not finish; and because of this, wrath came upon Israel, and the number was not included in the account of the chronicles of King David.
NASB.25: Now Azmaveth the son of Adiel had charge of the king's storehouses. And Jonathan the son of Uzziah had charge of the storehouses in the country, in the cities, in the villages and in the towers.
NASB.26: Ezri the son of Chelub had charge of the agricultural workers who tilled the soil.
NASB.27: Shimei the Ramathite had charge of the vineyards; and Zabdi the Shiphmite had charge of the produce of the vineyards [stored] in the wine cellars.
NASB.28: Baal-hanan the Gederite had charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the Shephelah; and Joash had charge of the stores of oil.
NASB.29: Shitrai the Sharonite had charge of the cattle which were grazing in Sharon; and Shaphat the son of Adlai had charge of the cattle in the valleys.
NASB.30: Obil the Ishmaelite had charge of the camels; and Jehdeiah the Meronothite had charge of the donkeys.
NASB.31: Jaziz the Hagrite had charge of the flocks. All these were overseers of the property which belonged to King David.
NASB.32: Also Jonathan, David's uncle, [was] a counselor, a man of understanding, and a scribe; and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni tutored the king's sons.
NASB.33: Ahithophel [was] counselor to the king; and Hushai the Archite [was] the king's friend.
NASB.34: Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar succeeded Ahithophel; and Joab was the commander of the king's army.

ESV.1: This is the number of the people of Israel, the heads of fathers' houses, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and their officers who served the king in all matters concerning the divisions that came and went, month after month throughout the year, each division numbering 24,000:
ESV.2: Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel was in charge of the first division in the first month; in his division were 24,000.
ESV.3: He was a descendant of Perez and was chief of all the commanders. He served for the first month.
ESV.4: Dodai the Ahohite  was in charge of the division of the second month; in his division were 24,000.
ESV.5: The third commander, for the third month, was Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada the chief priest; in his division were 24,000.
ESV.6: This is the Benaiah who was a mighty man of the thirty and in command of the thirty; Ammizabad his son was in charge of his division.
ESV.7: Asahel the brother of Joab was fourth, for the fourth month, and his son Zebadiah after him; in his division were 24,000.
ESV.8: The fifth commander, for the fifth month, was Shamhuth the Izrahite; in his division were 24,000.
ESV.9: Sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira, the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; in his division were 24,000.
ESV.10: Seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, of the sons of Ephraim; in his division were 24,000.
ESV.11: Eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites; in his division were 24,000.
ESV.12: Ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer of Anathoth, a Benjaminite; in his division were 24,000.
ESV.13: Tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai of Netophah, of the Zerahites; in his division were 24,000.
ESV.14: Eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah of Pirathon, of the sons of Ephraim; in his division were 24,000.
ESV.15: Twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel; in his division were 24,000.
ESV.16: Over the tribes of Israel, for the Reubenites, Eliezer the son of Zichri was chief officer; for the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maacah;
ESV.17: for Levi, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;
ESV.18: for Judah, Elihu, one of David's brothers; for Issachar, Omri the son of Michael;
ESV.19: for Zebulun, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jeremoth the son of Azriel;
ESV.20: for the Ephraimites, Hoshea the son of Azaziah; for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah;
ESV.21: for the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo the son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel the son of Abner;
ESV.22: for Dan, Azarel the son of Jeroham. These were the leaders of the tribes of Israel.
ESV.23: David did not count those below twenty years of age, for the LORD had promised to make Israel as many as the stars of heaven.
ESV.24: Joab the son of Zeruiah began to count, but did not finish. Yet wrath came upon Israel for this, and the number was not entered in the chronicles of King David.
ESV.25: Over the king's treasuries was Azmaveth the son of Adiel; and over the treasuries in the country, in the cities, in the villages, and in the towers, was Jonathan the son of Uzziah;
ESV.26: and over those who did the work of the field for tilling the soil was Ezri the son of Chelub;

NLT.1: This is the list of Israelite generals and captains, and their officers, who served the king by supervising the army divisions that were on duty each month of the year. Each division served for one month and had 24,000 troops.
NLT.2: Jashobeam son of Zabdiel was commander of the first division of 24,000 troops, which was on duty during the first month.
NLT.3: He was a descendant of Perez and was in charge of all the army officers for the first month.
NLT.4: Dodai, a descendant of Ahoah, was commander of the second division of 24,000 troops, which was on duty during the second month. Mikloth was his chief officer.
NLT.5: Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest was commander of the third division of 24,000 troops, which was on duty during the third month.
NLT.6: This was the Benaiah who commanded David’s elite military group known as the Thirty. His son Ammizabad was his chief officer.
NLT.7: Asahel, the brother of Joab, was commander of the fourth division of 24,000 troops, which was on duty during the fourth month. Asahel was succeeded by his son Zebadiah.
NLT.8: Shammah the Izrahite was commander of the fifth division of 24,000 troops, which was on duty during the fifth month.
NLT.9: Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa was commander of the sixth division of 24,000 troops, which was on duty during the sixth month.
NLT.10: Helez, a descendant of Ephraim from Pelon, was commander of the seventh division of 24,000 troops, which was on duty during the seventh month.
NLT.11: Sibbecai, a descendant of Zerah from Hushah, was commander of the eighth division of 24,000 troops, which was on duty during the eighth month.
NLT.12: Abiezer from Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin was commander of the ninth division of 24,000 troops, which was on duty during the ninth month.
NLT.13: Maharai, a descendant of Zerah from Netophah, was commander of the tenth division of 24,000 troops, which was on duty during the tenth month.
NLT.14: Benaiah from Pirathon in Ephraim was commander of the eleventh division of 24,000 troops, which was on duty during the eleventh month.
NLT.15: Heled, a descendant of Othniel from Netophah, was commander of the twelfth division of 24,000 troops, which was on duty during the twelfth month.
NLT.16:
The following were the tribes of Israel and their leaders: Tribe — Leader
Reuben — Eliezer son of Zicri
Simeon — Shephatiah son of Maacah
NLT.17:
Levi — Hashabiah son of Kemuel
Aaron (the priests) — Zadok
NLT.18:
Judah — Elihu (a brother of David)
Issachar — Omri son of Michael
NLT.19:
Zebulun — Ishmaiah son of Obadiah
Naphtali — Jeremoth son of Azriel
NLT.20:
Ephraim — Hoshea son of Azaziah
Manasseh (west) — Joel son of Pedaiah
NLT.21:
Manasseh in Gilead (east) — Iddo son of Zechariah
Benjamin — Jaasiel son of Abner
NLT.22:
Dan — Azarel son of Jeroham
These were the leaders of the tribes of Israel.
NLT.23: When David took his census, he did not count those who were younger than twenty years of age, because the LORD had promised to make the Israelites as numerous as the stars in heaven.
NLT.24: Joab son of Zeruiah began the census but never finished it because the anger of God fell on Israel. The total number was never recorded in King David’s official records.
NLT.25: Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the palace treasuries. Jonathan son of Uzziah was in charge of the regional treasuries throughout the towns, villages, and fortresses of Israel.
NLT.26: Ezri son of Kelub was in charge of the field workers who farmed the king’s lands.
NLT.27: Shimei from Ramah was in charge of the king’s vineyards. Zabdi from Shepham was responsible for the grapes and the supplies of wine.
NLT.28: Baal-hanan from Geder was in charge of the king’s olive groves and sycamore-fig trees in the foothills of Judah. Joash was responsible for the supplies of olive oil.
NLT.29: Shitrai from Sharon was in charge of the cattle on the Sharon Plain. Shaphat son of Adlai was responsible for the cattle in the valleys.
NLT.30: Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels. Jehdeiah from Meronoth was in charge of the donkeys.
NLT.31: Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the king’s flocks of sheep and goats. All these officials were overseers of King David’s property.
NLT.32: Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a wise counselor to the king, a man of great insight, and a scribe. Jehiel the Hacmonite was responsible for teaching the king’s sons.
NLT.33: Ahithophel was the royal adviser. Hushai the Arkite was the king’s friend.
NLT.34: Ahithophel was succeeded by Jehoiada son of Benaiah and by Abiathar. Joab was commander of the king’s army.

MSG.23: David didn't keep a count of men under the age of twenty, because God had promised to give Israel a population as numerous as the stars in the sky.
MSG.24: Joab son of Zeruiah started out counting the men, but he never finished. God's anger broke out on Israel because of the counting. As it turned out, the numbers were never entered into the court records of King David.
MSG.25: The king's storage facilities were supervised by Azmaveth son of Adiel. Jonathan son of Uzziah was responsible for the warehouses in the outlying areas.
MSG.26: Ezri son of Kelub was in charge of the field workers on the farms.
MSG.27: Shimei the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards and Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of grapes for the wine vats.
MSG.28: Baal-Hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive and sycamore-fig trees in the western hills, and Joash was in charge of the olive oil.
MSG.29: Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of herds grazing in Sharon and Shaphat son of Adlai was in charge of herds in the valley.
MSG.30: Obil the Ismaelite was in charge of the camels, Jehdeiah the Meronothite was in charge of the donkeys,
MSG.31: and Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the flocks. These were the ones responsible for taking care of King David's property.
MSG.32: Jonathan, David's uncle, a wise and literate counselor, and Jehiel son of Hacmoni, were responsible for rearing the king's sons.
MSG.33: Ahithophel was the king's counselor; Hushai the Arkite was the king's friend.
MSG.34: Ahithophel was later replaced by Jehoiada son of Benaiah and by Abiathar. Joab was commander of the king's army.

NRSVCE.1: This is the list of the people of Israel, the heads of families, the commanders of the thousands and the hundreds, and their officers who served the king in all matters concerning the divisions that came and went, month after month throughout the year, each division numbering twenty-four thousand:
NRSVCE.2: Jashobeam son of Zabdiel was in charge of the first division in the first month; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NRSVCE.3: He was a descendant of Perez, and was chief of all the commanders of the army for the first month.
NRSVCE.4: Dodai the Ahohite was in charge of the division of the second month; Mikloth was the chief officer of his division. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
NRSVCE.5: The third commander, for the third month, was Benaiah son of the priest Jehoiada, as chief; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NRSVCE.6: This is the Benaiah who was a mighty man of the Thirty and in command of the Thirty; his son Ammizabad was in charge of his division.
NRSVCE.7: Asahel brother of Joab was fourth, for the fourth month, and his son Zebadiah after him; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NRSVCE.8: The fifth commander, for the fifth month, was Shamhuth, the Izrahite; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NRSVCE.9: Sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NRSVCE.10: Seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, of the Ephraimites; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NRSVCE.11: Eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NRSVCE.12: Ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer of Anathoth, a Benjaminite; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NRSVCE.13: Tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai of Netophah, of the Zerahites; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NRSVCE.14: Eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah of Pirathon, of the Ephraimites; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NRSVCE.15: Twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
NRSVCE.16: Over the tribes of Israel, for the Reubenites, Eliezer son of Zichri was chief officer; for the Simeonites, Shephatiah son of Maacah;
NRSVCE.17: for Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;
NRSVCE.18: for Judah, Elihu, one of David’s brothers; for Issachar, Omri son of Michael;
NRSVCE.19: for Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel;
NRSVCE.20: for the Ephraimites, Hoshea son of Azaziah; for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah;
NRSVCE.21: for the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner;
NRSVCE.22: for Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These were the leaders of the tribes of Israel.
NRSVCE.23: David did not count those below twenty years of age, for the LORD had promised to make Israel as numerous as the stars of heaven.
NRSVCE.24: Joab son of Zeruiah began to count them, but did not finish; yet wrath came upon Israel for this, and the number was not entered into the account of the Annals of King David.
NRSVCE.25: Over the king’s treasuries was Azmaveth son of Adiel. Over the treasuries in the country, in the cities, in the villages and in the towers, was Jonathan son of Uzziah.
NRSVCE.26: Over those who did the work of the field, tilling the soil, was Ezri son of Chelub.
NRSVCE.27: Over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite. Over the produce of the vineyards for the wine cellars was Zabdi the Shiphmite.
NRSVCE.28: Over the olive and sycamore trees in the Shephelah was Baal-hanan the Gederite. Over the stores of oil was Joash.
NRSVCE.29: Over the herds that pastured in Sharon was Shitrai the Sharonite. Over the herds in the valleys was Shaphat son of Adlai.
NRSVCE.30: Over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite. Over the donkeys was Jehdeiah the Meronothite. Over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite.
NRSVCE.31: All these were stewards of King David’s property.
NRSVCE.32: Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, being a man of understanding and a scribe; Jehiel son of Hachmoni attended the king’s sons.
NRSVCE.33: Ahithophel was the king’s counselor, and Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend.
NRSVCE.34: After Ahithophel came Jehoiada son of Benaiah, and Abiathar. Joab was commander of the king’s army.

NET.1: What follows is a list of Israelite family leaders and commanders of units of a thousand and a hundred, as well as their officers who served the king in various matters. Each division was assigned to serve for one month during the year; each consisted of 24,000 men.
NET.2: Jashobeam son of Zabdiel was in charge of the first division, which was assigned the first month. His division consisted of 24,000 men.
NET.3: He was a descendant of Perez; he was in charge of all the army officers for the first month.
NET.4: Dodai the Ahohite was in charge of the division assigned the second month; Mikloth was the next in rank. His division consisted of 24,000 men.
NET.5: The third army commander, assigned the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest. He was the leader of his division, which consisted of 24,000 men.
NET.6: Benaiah was the leader of the thirty warriors and his division; his son was Ammizabad.
NET.7: The fourth, assigned the fourth month, was Asahel, brother of Joab; his son Zebadiah succeeded him. His division consisted of 24,000 men.
NET.8: The fifth, assigned the fifth month, was the commander Shamhuth the Izrahite. His division consisted of 24,000 men.
NET.9: The sixth, assigned the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. His division consisted of 24,000 men.
NET.10: The seventh, assigned the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, an Ephraimite. His division consisted of 24,000 men.
NET.11: The eighth, assigned the eighth month, was Sibbekai the Hushathite, a Zerahite. His division consisted of 24,000 men.
NET.12: The ninth, assigned the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, a Benjaminite. His division consisted of 24,000 men.
NET.13: The tenth, assigned the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, a Zerahite. His division consisted of 24,000 men.
NET.14: The eleventh, assigned the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, an Ephraimite. His division consisted of 24,000 men.
NET.15: The twelfth, assigned the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, a descendant of Othniel. His division consisted of 24,000 men.
NET.16: The officers of the Israelite tribes: Eliezer son of Zikri was the leader of the Reubenites, Shephatiah son of Maacah led the Simeonites,
NET.17: Hashabiah son of Kemuel led the Levites, Zadok led the descendants of Aaron,
NET.18: Elihu, a brother of David, led Judah, Omri son of Michael led Issachar,
NET.19: Ishmaiah son of Obadiah led Zebulun, Jerimoth son of Azriel led Naphtali,
NET.20: Hoshea son of Azaziah led the Ephraimites, Joel son of Pedaiah led the half-tribe of Manasseh,
NET.21: Iddo son of Zechariah led the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Jaasiel son of Abner led Benjamin,
NET.22: Azarel son of Jeroham led Dan. These were the commanders of the Israelite tribes.
NET.23: David did not count the males twenty years old and under, for the LORD had promised to make Israel as numerous as the stars in the sky.
NET.24: Joab son of Zeruiah started to count the men but did not finish. God was angry with Israel because of this, so the number was not recorded in the scroll called The Annals of King David.
NET.25: Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the king’s storehouses; Jonathan son of Uzziah was in charge of the storehouses in the field, in the cities, in the towns, and in the towers.
NET.26: Ezri son of Kelub was in charge of the field workers who farmed the land.
NET.27: Shimei the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards; Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of the wine stored in the vineyards.
NET.28: Baal-Hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the lowlands; Joash was in charge of the storehouses of olive oil.
NET.29: Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the cattle grazing in Sharon; Shaphat son of Adlai was in charge of the cattle in the valleys.
NET.30: Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels; Jehdeiah the Meronothite was in charge of the donkeys.
NET.31: Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the sheep. All these were the officials in charge of King David’s property.
NET.32: Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a wise adviser and scribe; Jehiel son of Hacmoni cared for the king’s sons.
NET.33: Ahithophel was the king’s adviser; Hushai the Arkite was the king’s confidant.
NET.34: Ahithophel was succeeded by Jehoiada son of Benaiah and by Abiathar. Joab was the commanding general of the king’s army.
